extracted.intended_audience: fiction authors (novelists and short-story writers) seeking developmental editing
extracted.subtask_description: Big-picture editorial evaluation of fiction manuscripts (novels and short stories), diagnosing structural, plot, character, pacing and voice issues and recommending revisions, delivered as reports, marked-up manuscripts, book maps and post-edit support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story idea / premise
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this a good idea for a story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A developmental editor may suggest that the premise on which the book is written needs tweaking or adjusting; part of 'big picture' editing is determining whether the central idea is viable and productive for a full manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the plot and structure create a good foundation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The edit looks at the shape of the plot and the manuscript as a whole; the editor may recommend moving, deleting, or rewriting whole passages or chapters if the structure is weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and event regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do things happen regularly enough and with the right amount of tension?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether events are distributed to maintain reader interest; if pacing is harmed by too much description or uneven event distribution the editor will point to where and suggest solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplot effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the subplots work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether subplots support the main story, are integrated appropriately, and contribute to overall momentum and thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward motion / conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there forward motion through conflicts or adequately challenging obstacles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether scenes and sequences propel the story via conflict and obstacles rather than stalling; looks for clear stakes and escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the characters engage the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether characters capture reader interest, have distinctive presence, and elicit emotional or intellectual investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character believability and motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are they believable? Do their motivations make sense and are they strong enough?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses internal consistency, plausibility and strength of character drives; may recommend deeper motivation, clearer arcs or trimming characters who don't serve the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension / downtime balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a good amount of tension? And some downtime too?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks rhythm between high-tension scenes and quieter moments so the reader is not fatigued or numbed by constant intensity; recommends adjustments to restore balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening engagement and closing satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the opening chapter engage? Does the closing chapter satisfy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the opening hooks readers and establishes necessary elements, and whether the ending provides resolution, payoff, or appropriate emotional closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of narrative techniques (scenes, dialogue, voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well are certain narrative techniques used? For example, are there enough scenes, is the dialogue well placed, and is the voice consistent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses scene construction, dialogue placement and function, and voice consistency across chapters/POVs; may recommend restructuring scenes, trimming or adding dialogue, or unifying voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language ticks and repetitive habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the writer have certain language ticks (words or techniques they love and use a bit too regularly) that end up being distracting for the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies recurring words, phrases or stylistic habits that distract; points to instances in the manuscript and suggests alternatives or strategies to reduce repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure (editorial report focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial report examines structure as a heading alongside theme, story and character development and point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides a detailed, labelled analysis (10–15 pages) of structural problems and suggests solutions, often accompanied by a book map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme (editorial report focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial report evaluates theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses how thematic material is developed or diluted through plot and character choices and recommends strengthening or clarifying themes where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story development (editorial report focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial report looks at story development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies gaps, uneven development or logic problems in the story arc and suggests structural or scene-level fixes to improve development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development (editorial report focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial report examines character development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lists of characters with notes on attributes and tracks arcs, inconsistencies and opportunities for development; recommends revisions for fuller or clearer arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view (editorial report focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial report assesses point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks for consistent and effective POV choices, problems with head-hopping, and whether POV serves voice and reader understanding; suggests consolidation or clarity where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem identification and suggested solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial report 'identifies and analyses problems and suggests possible solutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report is diagnostic and prescriptive: it points to issues, analyses their cause/effect, and proposes multiple options for repair rather than only flagging faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and setting inventories with post-revision assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Report includes lists of characters and settings with notes of their attributes and an assessment of what the manuscript may need after the suggested revisions are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete inventories to help track elements across revisions and an anticipated next-stage plan after major revisions are implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinpointed manuscript edits (fully marked-up manuscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully marked-up manuscript: page edits using track changes and comments pinpoint areas highlighted in the editorial report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks exact locations where problems occur (e.g., excessive description affecting pace), offers inline suggestions and examples to guide the writer in applying report recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book map (scene-by-scene analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table showing analysis of the book, scene by scene, chapter by chapter (book map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to visualise overall shape, locate problematic sections, plan large moves (e.g., moving a chapter), and assist in rewriting when substantial structural changes are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-editing support
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving feedback, included support is either a one-hour meeting (video/phone) or one email answering further questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides clarification, deeper explanation of suggested revisions, and targeted coaching during the revision process to help authors implement changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service level differentiation: full developmental edit vs manuscript critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Two services differ in depth, time, cost and deliverables: Full Developmental Edit (editorial report, fully marked-up manuscript, book map, post-editing support) vs Manuscript Critique (editorial report, book map, post-editing support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on which to choose: full edit is for those who 'know very little about the craft' or want detailed, hands-on attention; a manuscript critique suits writers who 'know a fair amount' and want an overview or are on a tight budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental editing for short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories can be looked at in terms of story structure and character; the edit will include a short report and a marked-up manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service adapts the big-picture approach to short-form fiction, focusing on compressed structure, economy of detail and concise character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial developmental edit (focused aspect edit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial developmental edit: examine only one aspect of your novel (e.g., plot) at a lower price than a full developmental edit or manuscript critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when a single area has received negative feedback or when the author wants targeted input rather than a full sweep.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to seek a developmental edit (decision criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: You might need a developmental edit if: you feel there are problems with plot or character but don't know how to fix them; feedback from groups/beta readers has been negative, contradictory or not specific enough; you are a first-time author who has not studied craft; you want to study fiction using your own work; you want to ensure story foundations are stable before line- and copy-editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scenarios indicate foundational or structural uncertainty where a big-picture external perspective can save time and prevent polishing a fundamentally flawed draft.
